Interface IuOidcClaimsSource

public interface IuOidcClaimsSource
Supplies the claims an OpenID Provider asserts about one end user.

The seam between a provider endpoint and whatever holds identity data. A deployment implements this over its own directory, database, or attribute service; the endpoint asks it for a principal and never learns where the answer came from. That keeps an identity service free of OpenID Connect — it neither verifies tokens nor knows which relying party is asking — while the provider keeps the parts that are its own: which of the claims OpenID Connect defines a grant's scope admits, which token they are being written to, and how what it publishes is signed and encrypted.

Disclosure is decided in two halves

The claims OpenID Connect §5.4 binds to profile, email, address and phone are fixed by specification, so the provider maps those itself and an implementation never reasons about them. Every other scope is the deployment's own, and so are the claims it releases — admitted is where that half is decided, and it sees only the scopes §5.4 does not cover.

A scope a deployment defines only reaches here if some client resource registers it. An authorization request asking for a scope no resource grants is refused as invalid_scope before any of this is consulted.

  • Method Details

    • admitted

      Set<String> admitted(Set<String> scope, IuOidcClaimsSource.Usage usage)
      Names the §5.1.2 Additional Claims this source releases for scopes OpenID Connect does not define.

      Only the deployment's own scopes arrive here; the sets §5.4 binds to profile, email, address and phone are the provider's to map and are added to whatever this answers. A scope this source doesn't know releases nothing, the same way an unrecognized §5.4 scope does.

      Whatever is named here is passed back as admittedClaims on the next call, so a name answered for one IuOidcClaimsSource.Usage and withheld for another is how a source keeps a claim out of a durable ID token while still publishing it from UserInfo.

      Parameters:
      scope - scopes the grant was authorized for, less those OpenID Connect §5.4 defines a claim set for; empty if it asked for none of the deployment's own
      usage - where the claims named here are about to be published
      Returns:
      claim names this source releases for scope at usage; empty, never null, to release nothing
      See Also:
      • OpenID Connect Core 1.0 §5.1.2

    • claims

      void claims(String principalName, Set<String> admittedClaims, edu.iu.jwt.WebTokenBuilder builder)
      Writes the claims this source holds for one principal onto a token this provider is issuing.

      A token carries typed claims rather than a rendered document, so this writes rather than returning: WebTokenBuilder.claim(String, Object, java.lang.reflect.Type) takes each value with the type it is to serialize as, which is what keeps updated_at a NumericDate and address a nested object without the provider having any opinion about either. IuOidcClaims names what those types are for the claims OpenID Connect defines; this source is what applies them.

      Write nothing but admittedClaims. A claim named there and not held is simply omitted, and a claim held but not named is withheld — the set is what the grant's scope admits, so writing past it discloses what was never authorized. The registered claims a token is identified by, and those the provider derives for itself, are written after this returns and are not a source's to set.

      Parameters:
      principalName - principal name the provider has settled from a verified grant, and the sub the token already names
      admittedClaims - names of the claims to write; empty to write none
      builder - token being issued

    • claims

      edu.iu.oidc.IuOidcClaims claims(String principalName, Set<String> admittedClaims)
      Gets the claims this source holds for one principal, rendered as the document an unsigned UserInfo response publishes.

      The answer is what a provider publishes, so toString() must render it as that claims document — a deployment configures the rendering for itself, and the provider publishes the result without looking at it. IuOidcClaims is what states the shape it has to render to.

      Only an unsigned UserInfo response reaches here. A signed one is a JWT, and is built through claims(String, Set, WebTokenBuilder) like any other token this provider issues — which is also where the iss and aud OpenID Connect §5.3.2 requires a signed response to carry come from, written by the provider rather than rendered by this source. A plain document has nothing to lift out of a response and carries neither.

      Parameters:
      principalName - principal name the provider has settled from a verified grant, and the sub the rendered document must name. The provider does not read it back to check: a source that resolves a principal name to some other form — a username for a numeric ID, say — breaks the comparison a relying party makes against the ID token it holds
      admittedClaims - names of the claims the grant admits: the §5.4 sets its scope covers, sub among them when openid was granted, plus whatever admitted(Set, Usage) named for IuOidcClaimsSource.Usage.USERINFO. Anything else this source holds is not to be answered
      Returns:
      claims held for principalName, limited to admittedClaims, rendering as a claims document
      See Also:
      • OpenID Connect Core 1.0 §5.3.2
